correctness.rationale: The equality of classical Milnor numbers follows from explicit Weierstrass length and a Cohen–Macaulay parameter argument. Both Jacobian ideals are parameter complete intersections, so all syzygies are Koszul. Truncating at k=b-1 yields syzygy image ranks 2r and 2r+1, because xz^(k-2) is not divisible by x^(a-1); hence the difference is exactly -1 in every parameter case. Five independent finite-rank checks agree but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A uniform explicit counterexample to a published higher-Milnor rigidity conjecture is a substantive boundary result: the same ordinary Milnor number persists, yet one new ordinary m-adic Koszul syzygy direction reduces a higher Milnor number exactly by one. The family identifies an algebraic mechanism and pinpoints a failure outside the recent equal-weight theorem.
